clue.text: Plastered, so gave up

blocks.note: first meaning: coated a wall with a layer of plaster or cement
second meaning: handed over or surrendered

explanation.surface: Someone got so drunk that they gave up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' reads as drunk, but here it is the builder's sense of coating a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To render a wall is to coat it with plaster, and to render something can also mean to surrender or hand it over.

clue.text: Store a vehicle's outside measurement

indicators.note: one thing being outside another means it wraps around it

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
an ell is an old measure of length for cloth

explanation.surface: Someone wants to know the outer dimensions of a car before storing it.
explanation.walkthrough: An ell is an old English cloth measure of about 45 inches.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar is an underground room used for keeping wine, coal or other goods in storage.

clue.text: Stuff obtainable for ready money only

blocks.note: ready money is cash in hand
mere means only, nothing more than

explanation.surface: A shop notice: these goods are sold for cash only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' here is the old word for woven fabric, not things in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old name for woven cloth, and cashmere is a fine woollen fabric made from goat hair.

clue.text: Very large bloom once highly esteemed by Egyptians

blocks.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
an iris is a flower

explanation.surface: A huge flower was prized by the ancient Egyptians.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the lotus or papyrus; the definition is a whole phrase pointing at a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was a major deity of ancient Egypt, god of the dead and the afterlife, so was worshipped there in antiquity.

clue.text: About fifty always present smart appearance

blocks.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
as in ever-present, ever means always

explanation.surface: A man of about fifty who always looks well turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart appearance' looks like one phrase about clothes; only 'smart' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart in the sense of quick-witted and intelligent is a direct synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Appalling cad - and he's run after!

indicators.note: something appalling is in a dreadful state, so these letters are a mess to be sorted

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A dreadful bounder is pursued, to general approval.
explanation.walkthrough: A cad is an old word for a dishonourable man.
explanation.definitionFit: Chased is the past participle of chase, meaning pursued, which is exactly what being run after is.

clue.text: Romans required money to get free

indicators.note: read as re-quired, the letters are worked over afresh into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Romans demanded payment before releasing a captive.
explanation.definitionFit: A ransom is the payment demanded for releasing a kidnapped person or captured property.

clue.text: Deplores doctors hanging around the tea maker

indicators.note: things hanging around something gather on either side of it

blocks.note: MO is a medical officer, so doctors are MOS
a tea urn makes tea for a crowd

explanation.surface: Someone disapproves of doctors loitering by the tea urn instead of working.
explanation.walkthrough: MO, medical officer, is the army term for a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To mourn is to lament or grieve over something, close in sense to deploring it.

clue.text: Place to get drink? That's an idea!

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
a position is a place

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a spot to go for a drink, and another approves.
explanation.walkthrough: The place 'gets' the drink placed in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A supposition is an assumption or hypothesis, a notion held without proof.

clue.text: A little Bach and Elgar maybe - or some other composer

indicators.note: only a small part of the following words is wanted, sitting inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first name, the middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A playlist of some Bach and Elgar, or maybe another composer.
explanation.walkthrough: bacH AND ELgar contains the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel was a German-born Baroque composer who worked in London, famous for Messiah.

clue.text: Superior woman to crush and escort to the door

blocks.note: U means upper-class, socially superior
she is a woman
to rout is to defeat utterly

explanation.surface: A haughty woman flattens someone and shows them out.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher someone out is to lead them politely from a room, guiding them out through the exit.

clue.text: Bring up the right to a listening device

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
the ear is the organ we listen with

explanation.surface: Someone raises the matter of rights with a bugging device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring up' suggests raising a topic; here it means raising children.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear children or animals is to raise them, looking after them until they are grown.

clue.text: Dealing with urgent checking

blocks.note: re means concerning or about
a pressing matter is urgent

explanation.surface: Handling an urgent check, like an inspector on a deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: Checking in the sense of restraining or holding back is what repressing does to feelings or dissent.

clue.text: Youngsters like receiving handout - small change

indicators.note: something receiving another takes it inside itself

blocks.note: as means like
the dole is state benefit paid out
cents are coins of small value

explanation.surface: Young people resemble those getting a handout, a few coins.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is the British name for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolescents are teenagers, young people between childhood and adult life.

clue.text: The student meriting education

blocks.note: L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates
earning praise is meriting it

explanation.surface: The student who deserves to be educated.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is the knowledge acquired through study, which is what an education provides.

clue.text: Take a revolutionary step in attempt to procure material

indicators.note: a revolution overturns the existing order, so the letters are turned upside down
one part is put inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A radical move is attempted to get hold of some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary step' looks like one phrase for a radical move; the first word only tells you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapestry is a heavy woven fabric with pictures or designs, so it is a kind of textile.

clue.text: Derby cricket team member

blocks.note: first meaning: a derby is the American name for a round hard felt hat
second meaning: a player who delivers the ball in cricket

explanation.surface: A player in Derbyshire's county cricket side.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby looks like the English town with a county cricket club; it is the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The derby hat is called by another name in Britain, and the same word names the cricketer who sends the ball at the batsman.

clue.text: Say there's point to everything, for example

blocks.note: all means everything
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'
E is east, a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone claims there is a purpose to everything, as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' suggests a purpose; here it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert or claim something, usually without proof, which is one sense of say.

clue.text: Businessman set against a player losing his head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is lost

blocks.note: contra is Latin for against
an actor plays a part

explanation.surface: A businessman opposes a performer who has lost his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTOR loses its first letter to give CTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A contractor is a person or firm that undertakes paid work, such as building jobs, under contract.

clue.text: A large number entering the examination appear extremely dull

indicators.note: something entering goes inside another part

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: Many people sitting an exam look thoroughly bored.
explanation.walkthrough: A and M go inside TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamest is the superlative of tame, meaning the most lacking in excitement or interest.

clue.text: Stranger calling for a big glass

blocks.note: first meaning: more odd, using the British slang adjective rum for odd
second meaning: a large old-fashioned drinking goblet

explanation.surface: An unknown visitor orders a large drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' reads as a newcomer but is the comparative adjective; rum is British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum means odd, so rummer means odder, and a rummer is also a large stemmed drinking cup.

clue.text: The tiresome person parking badly

blocks.note: P is the road-sign symbol for parking
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: That annoying driver has parked badly again.
explanation.definitionFit: Pill is informal slang for a boring or irritating individual.

clue.text: Flighty creature in the pink and burning with love

blocks.note: flaming means on fire
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A frivolous person in excellent health and passionately in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' and 'in the pink' suggest a giddy, healthy person; they describe a pink bird that flies.
explanation.definitionFit: The flamingo is a pink wading bird that can fly, so a pink flying creature fits.

clue.text: Filmed first in the Mediterranean

indicators.note: one part sits inside the other

blocks.note: 1st, with the digit read as the letter I
the Med is the usual short name for the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: A movie was shot for the first time on the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filmed' suggests a camera; it means covered with a thin film, as of condensation.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass that has misted over is covered with a thin layer of droplets, so it has been filmed over.

clue.text: Object to being ordered to go again

blocks.note: first meaning: feel bitter about
second meaning: ..., dispatched a second time

explanation.surface: Someone protests at being told to go back once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent is to feel aggrieved by, and re-sent means dispatched a second time.

clue.text: Late transport here's a problem

indicators.note: a problem is something to be worked out, so the letters must be sorted

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A delayed bus or train is causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' reads as behind schedule; it means dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearse is the vehicle carrying a coffin, so it conveys the deceased.
